html:
A Greek churchman and scholar who backed union with Rome, became a cardinal, and moved to Italy, where he helped bring Greek learning into the Renaissance.

Born in Trebizond, he studied under Gemistos Plethon at Mistra and became archbishop of Nicaea. At the Council of Florence in 1439 he was one of the main Greek voices for union. Pope Eugene IV made him a cardinal that year, and he spent the rest of his life in Italy. He was nearly elected pope.

He gathered Greek scholars around him and wrote a defence of Plato against critics. After the fall of Constantinople he worked to save Greek books and urged a crusade. In 1468 he gave his library of about a thousand manuscripts to Venice. It became the core of the Marciana Library, which still holds it.
